'''Marcus Anthony Georges-Hunt''' (born March 28, 1994) is an American-U.S. Virgin Islander professional [[basketball]] player for [[Al Riyadi Club Beirut|Al Riyadi]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]]. He played college basketball for [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]]. {{Short description|American basketball player (born 1994)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2024}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Marcus Georges-Hunt | image = Marcus Georges-Hunt.jpg | caption = Georges-Hunt playing for Georgia Tech Basketball Club | position = [[Shooting guard]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 6 | weight_lb = 220 | league = [[Lebanese Basketball League]] | team = [[Al Riyadi Club Beirut|Al Riyadi]] | number = 94 | nationality = American / U.S. Virgin Islander | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1994|3|28}} | birth_place = [[Miami, Florida]], U.S. | high_school = [[North Clayton High School|North Clayton]]
([[College Park, Georgia]]) | college = [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] (2012–2016) | draft_year = 2016 | career_start = 2016 | years1 = 2016–2017 | team1 = [[Maine Red Claws]] | years2 = {{nbay|2016|end}} | team2 = [[Orlando Magic]] | years3 = {{nbay|2017|full=y}} | team3 = [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] | years4 = 2017 | team4 = →[[Iowa Wolves]] | years5 = 2018 | team5 = Maine Red Claws | years6 = 2019–2020 | team6 = [[Guangzhou Loong Lions]] | years7 = 2020–2021 | team7 = [[Sichuan Blue Whales]] | years8 = [[2021-22 NBA G League season|2022]] | team8 = [[College Park Skyhawks]] | years9 = 2022 | team9 = [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] | years10 = 2022–2024 | team10 = [[Kuwait SC (basketball)|Kuwait SC]] | years11 = 2024 | team11 = [[Shabab Al Ahli Club (basketball)|Shabab Al Ahli]] | years12 = 2024–2025 | team12 = Sichuan Blue Whales | years13 = 2025 | team13 = [[Al Riyadi Club Beirut|Al Riyadi]] | years14 = 2026 | team14 = [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]] | years15 = 2026–present | team15 = [[Al Riyadi Club Beirut|Al Riyadi]] | highlights = * [[BCL Asia]] Tournament Top Five ([[2024 Basketball Champions League Asia|2024]]) * [[FIBA West Asia Super League|WASL champion]] ([[2024–25 FIBA West Asia Super League|2025]]) * [[Arab Club Basketball Championship]] winner ([[2022 Arab Club Basketball Championship|2022]]) * [[Lebanese Basketball League|Lebanese Basketball League]] winner (2025) *[[All-NBA Development League Team|All-NBA D-League Third Team]] (2017) *[[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star]] (2017) *Second-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] – Coaches (2016) *Third-team All-ACC – Media (2016) }} ==High school career== Georges-Hunt attended [[North Clayton High School]] under coach Martisse Troup. As a senior, he averaged 24.2 points, 14.3 rebounds and 5.2 assists helping the Eagles to a 21–11 record and a berth in the state semifinals. When he graduated, he was North Clayton's all-time leading scorer with 2,189 points and was considered a 4-star recruit, being ranked No. 59 overall in the ESPN100, and No. 14 among small forwards.{{cite web|url=http://www.ramblinwreck.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/marcus_georges_hunt_819226.html|title=Marcus Georges-Hunt bio|work=RamblinWreck.com|access-date=October 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161223015308/http://www.ramblinwreck.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/marcus_georges_hunt_819226.html|archive-date=December 23, 2016|url-status=dead}} ==College career== After graduating high school, Georges-Hunt played college basketball for [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets basketball|Georgia Tech]]. He was a starter for the Yellow Jackets all four years, but injured his foot as a junior and missed some time. During his senior season, he led the team to the [[2016 National Invitation Tournament]] after a 12–19 record the year prior. He averaged 16.9 points per game as a senior.{{cite news|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/02/25/sports/ncaabasketball/georgia-tech-marcus-georges-hunt.html?_r=0|title=Georgia Tech Senior's Belief Finally Translates to Wins|work=[[New York Times]]|date=February 25, 2016|access-date=August 29, 2016}} Georges-Hunt was named to the Third Team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]].{{cite news|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/acsma-announces-basketball-season-awards-all-acc-teams-03-06-2016|title=ACSMA Announces Basketball Postseason Awards, All-ACC Teams|publisher=theacc.com|author=Press Release|date=March 6, 2016|access-date=March 6, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307040403/http://www.theacc.com/news/acsma-announces-basketball-season-awards-all-acc-teams-03-06-2016|archive-date=March 7, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Maine Red Claws (2016–2017)=== After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Georges-Hunt joined the [[Brooklyn Nets]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]]. In four games for the Nets, he averaged 2.8 points and 1.0 rebounds in 13.2 minutes per game. On September 26, 2016, he signed with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-finalize-training-camp-roster-1|title=Celtics Finalize Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2016|access-date=September 26, 2016}} However, he was later waived by the Celtics on October 20, 2016, after appearing in two preseason games.{{cite tweet|number=789206808367726594|user=celtics|title=The Celtics have waived Marcus Georges-Hunt, Damion Lee and Jalen Jones. |accessdate=October 20, 2016|date=October 20, 2016}} On October 31, 2016, he was acquired by the [[Maine Red Claws]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Celtics.{{cite web|url=http://maine.dleague.nba.com/news/2016-training-camp-roster/|title=2016 Training Camp Roster Announced|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=November 2, 2016|archive-date=November 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104004654/http://maine.dleague.nba.com/news/2016-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}} ===Miami Heat (2017)=== On February 8, 2017, Georges-Hunt signed a 10-day contract with the [[Miami Heat]]{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/newsrecap/heat-signs-marcus-georges-hunt|title=HEAT Signs Marcus Georges-Hunt|work=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2017|access-date=February 8, 2017}} to help the team deal with numerous injuries. Miami had to use an NBA hardship exemption in order to sign him as he made their roster stand at 16, being one player over the allowed limited of 15.{{cite web|last=Winderman|first=Ira|url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/sfl-miami-heat-josh-richardson-s020817-story.html|title=Heat add former Georgia Tech guard Marcus Georges-Hunt on 10-day contract|work=Sun-Sentinel.com|date=February 8, 2017|access-date=February 8, 2017}} On February 16, he was assigned to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] so he could participate in the NBA Development League All-Star Game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/white-and-georges-hunt-play-nba-development-league-all-star-game|title=White And Georges-Hunt To Play In NBA Development League All-Star Game|work=NBA.com|date=February 16, 2017|access-date=February 22, 2017}} On February 18, after the 10-day contract expired,{{cite web|last=Winderman|first=Ira|url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-okaro-white-021917-story.html|title=Georges-Hunt's Heat 10-day contract expires; Okaro White has |url-status=dead }} ===Orlando Magic (2017)=== On April 3, 2017, Georges-Hunt signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite (2017–2018)=== On August 11, 2017, Georges-Hunt signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-marcus-georges-hunt|title=TIMBERWOLVES SIGN recalled by the Timberwolves the next day.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-recall-marcus-georges-hunt-nba-g-league-affiliate-iowa-wolves|title=TIMBERWOLVES RECALL MARCUS GEORGES-HUNT FROM NBA G LEAGUE AFFILIATE IOWA WOLVES|work=NBA.com|date=November 10, 2017|access-date=January 20, 2018}} On January 20, 2018, he had career highs in points (12) and minutes (29) in the He played a total of 42 games for Minnesota{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975426|title=Wiggins scores 29 as Wolves rally past Raptors 115–109|work=ESPN.com|date=January 20, 2018|access-date=January 20, 2018}} ===Return to Maine (2018)=== On October 1, 2018, Georges-Hunt signed with the [[Boston Celtics]] to a training camp deal.{{cite news |last1=Westerholm |first1=Tom |url=https://www.pressherald.com/2018/10/19/fridays-sports-digest-red-claws-make-moves-before-g-league-draft/ |access-date=October 22, 2018 |work=[[Portland Press-Herald]] |date=October 19, 2018}} 2018. ===College Park Skyhawks (2022)=== On January 14, 2022, Georges-Hunt signed an [[NBA G League]] contract and was then acquired off-waivers by the [[College Park Skyhawks]]{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021–22 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 14, 2022|access-date=January 14, 2022}} where he averaged 13.4 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3 assists in 28 games.{{cite tweet|author=La Guerra del BSN|number=1526724277030031361|title=#BSNPR OFICIAL: El delantero Marcus Georges-Hunt (6'6) es el nuevo refuerzo de los Mets de Guaynabo en sustitución de Zach Hankins. Georges-Hunt viene de promediar 13.4 PPG, 5.3 RPG y 3 APG en 28 juegos con College Park en la G-League.|user=LaGuerraBSN|date=May 17, 2022|access-date=May 23, 2022}} ===Mets de Guaynabo (2022)=== On May 17, 2022, Georges-Hunt signed with [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN). Georges-Hunt joined the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612737/hawks |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} === Kuwait Club (2022–2023) === In October 2022, he played with [[Kuwait SC (basketball)|Kuwait]] in the [[2022 Arab Club Basketball Championship]]. Georges-Hunt helped Kuwait SC win their first-ever Arab championship.{{Cite web |title=KUNA : Kuwait SC wins Arab Club Basketball trophy - Sports - 15/10/2022 |url=https://www.kuna.net.kw/ArticleDetails.aspx?id=3059791&language=en |access-date=2022-10-16 |website=www.kuna.net.kw}} On May 15, 2023, Georges-Hunt proved crucial in Kuwait Club's capture of the inaugural [[West Asia Super League|WASL]] Gulf League championship, as he scored a season-high 35 points in the decisive second game of the finals.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-15 |title=Undefeated Kuwait Club fulfill destiny, emerge as inaugural WASL-Gulf champions |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/wasl/22-23/gulf/news/undefeated-kuwait-club-fulfill-destiny-emerge-as-inaugural-wasl-gulf-champions |access-date=2023-09-29 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} === Shabab Al Ahli (2024) === Georges-Hunt helped [[Shabab Al Ahli Club (basketball)|Shabab Al Ahli]] finish runners-up in the [[2024 Basketball Champions League Asia]], and was named to the Tournament Best Five after the lost final.{{Cite web |title=Wael Arakji named Basketball Champions League Asia 2024 MVP |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/bclasia/2024/news/wael-arakji-named-basketball-champions-league-asia-2024-mvp |access-date=2024-06-17 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} ===Sichuan Blue Whales (2024-2025)=== On September 20, 2024, Georges-Hunt signed to the [[Sichuan Blue Whales]]. He was the second foreign player in the roster as [[Edmond Sumner]] signed there earlier. It was his comeback to the Blue Whales as he played there in 2020–2021.{{cite web |title=Georges-Hunt signs at Blue Whales |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/892051/Georges-Hunt-signs-at-Blue-Whales |website=www.asia-basket.com |access-date=20 September 2024}} ===Al Riyadi (2025)=== On April 1, 2025, Georges-Hunt signed with [[Al Riyadi Club Beirut|Al Riyadi]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].{{cite web |title=Al Riyadi adds Georges-Hunt to their roster |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/news/926363/Al-Riyadi-adds-Georges-Hunt-to-their-roster |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=April 1, 2025 |date=April 1, 2025}} He won the [[2024–25 FIBA West Asia Super League]] with Al Riyadi, and contributed 24 points and 5 rebounds in the championship game.{{Cite web |date=2025-05-18 |title=History made as Al Riyadi complete FIBA WASL back-to-back
